title: Progress / Learning
author: clean_rebel29
selftext:
Hello! 

I'm back again with an update. This is genuinely a personal project / hobby project. I don't really have any intentions on releasing what's shown here at least not anytime soon or for it to be anything serious. 

Goal: Souls-like difficulty and combat in an ARPG style game that also lets you zoom into over the shoulder perspective. I also want to create a simple skill tree that works something like the skill-tree in Skyrim so that you're not locked to a single play-style or class. Lastly, I want the atmosphere to be fantasy (sometimes dark) but not a horror fantasy I've been getting tired of that so I figured I'd just build this for fun. 

Disclaimer: I know the game is SUPER ROUGH. There's a million things I need to do before I could even call this 10% of the way there. But just felt like sharing what I've learned below. 

Background: I'm a software developer began full-time work back in 2011 with a background in Computer Engineering & Computer Science. GameDev is NOT my career or profession. 

Tools: Astra Codex, Godot with MCP, [Blender with MCP](https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/), Free Assets from various stores online and [Mixamo ](https://www.mixamo.com/)for  rigging and animating said assets.   
  
What I've learned:  

* **Architecture:** Planning out your code base is everything! If you're not a programmer its definitely worth looking up the different design patterns for the tools you're using! In my case with Godot being an object oriented language I was worth looking into the various object oriented programming design patterns. For example I have A LOT of [composition ](https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/composition-vs-inheritance)this makes the spell / skill system quite flexible with different damage types, different attack speeds, and different modifiers like buffs vs de-buffs without the code getting too sloppy! I probably spent an entire week just thinking about the way I want to organize this entire game's system before writing any code (or prompting any code) but in return you'll save so much headache in the future. 
* **Automate / Script** all repetitive tasks! It will save you tokens and it will save you time! For my game I have an "Asset Pipeline" and a "Architecture Pipeline". The purpose of the "Architecture Pipeline" is for whenever you give your AI Tool a prompt be it Codex, Claude Code etc.. it does not waste time, tokens, and context reading your entire code base! Not only should your code base be well organized with proper design patters as spoke about above but you should consider creating a system where your AI tools can query the code base and immediately get all the data for a specific object it needs back. 
   * For a request such as “Update the bow attack,” Codex can use the architecture pipeline to locate bow-related code, identify its owning systems, and inspect known dependencies, callers, source locations, and linked documentation. File outlines expose function names, signatures, line ranges, and documented purposes, allowing Codex to read the relevant sections without opening entire files. This provides a focused starting point for understanding the change; runtime behavior still requires separate verification.
   * The asset pipeline complements this by providing targeted asset inspection, animation inventory and role assignments, curated motion labels, naming validation, and repeatable preparation and review workflows. Its records describe asset availability and configuration; they do not establish whether an asset actually plays during gameplay.
* **Harness / Documentation:** Setup a "Agents.md" or whatever you want to call the documentation to act as a "Harness" for the prompts you're giving the AI tools. Having the harness / documentation be the entry point for each prompt sets a standard of what design patterns, "vocabulary" as it pertains to your game's system, and naming conventions, the AI tool should always use. 
* **Focus Small:** Work in small chunks. Iterate slowly, it'll save you time, it'll save you tokens, and it'll over-all just look a lot better. This is probably my main weakness... I always get too ambitious and try to do too many things at once. This is true for Software Development professionally but can probably apply to basically any task in life. 

TRUST ME it will save you a lot of time and headache. If you're not familiar with software and programming that's okay, learn a few of the things above. 

IF you are familiar with programming and you have any suggestions for me or think what I wrote above is complete nonsense I'm all ears! 

As far as 3D art animation rigging etc... all goes I'm still learning so I probably should refrain from giving advice on that.
